patterns.name: Disco 1
patterns.notes: Tambourine on the offbeats is the whole disco trick.

patterns.name: Disco 2
patterns.notes: Cowbell answering the tambourine.

patterns.name: House 78
patterns.notes: House frame using tambourine where an open hat would go.

patterns.name: Deep House 78
patterns.notes: Soft and shuffly, bongo filling the gaps.

patterns.name: Nu-Disco 78
patterns.notes: Stuttered hats plus maraca sixteenths.

patterns.name: Italo 78
patterns.notes: Cowbell answer phrase in the back half of the bar.

patterns.name: Cosmic Disco
patterns.notes: Cowbell in threes over a straight four — the accent lane follows the bell.

patterns.name: Motorik 78
patterns.notes: Neu! pulse on the Beat Bot. Strict.

patterns.name: Krautrock Shuffle
patterns.notes: Motorik with the shuffle knob at 44 — it lopes.

patterns.name: Steppers
patterns.notes: Four-to-the-floor reggae. Kick tuned deep.

patterns.name: Minimal 78
patterns.notes: Sparse to the point of rudeness. Strict.

patterns.name: Balearic
patterns.notes: Sunset tempo, guiro scrape as the hook.

patterns.name: Foxtrot
patterns.notes: Stiff ballroom four. Strict, as the original was.

patterns.name: Tambourine Pulse
patterns.notes: Sixteenth tambourine with accents wandering by bar.

patterns.name: Cowbell Drive
patterns.notes: More cowbell. Non-negotiable.

patterns.name: Guiro Groove
patterns.notes: Long and short guiro traded against each other.

patterns.name: Tresillo
patterns.notes: The 3-3-2 kick against son clave, which is where the figure comes from in the first place.

patterns.name: Tresillo Cumbia
patterns.notes: Tresillo kick under a guiro ostinato. The long and short scrapes pull against the kick.

patterns.name: Half Tresillo
patterns.notes: Three kicks a bar with a tumbao underneath - the most space of the tresillo set.

patterns.name: Dembow 78
patterns.notes: Dembow with the tambourine on the offbeats.

patterns.name: Baile 78
patterns.notes: Tamborzão figure on the congas.

patterns.name: Samba
patterns.notes: Surdo kick, caixa snare, agogô-style cowbell.

patterns.name: Soukous
patterns.notes: Fast, bright, congas chattering.

patterns.name: Merengue
patterns.notes: Fast tambora-style snare, güira running eighths.

patterns.name: Cumbia
patterns.notes: Long and short guiro strokes doing the cumbia limp.

patterns.name: Bomba
patterns.notes: Sicá-flavoured bomba figure.

patterns.name: Highlife
patterns.notes: Bell in threes against the four.

patterns.name: Afro House 78
patterns.notes: Threes stacked over a straight four.

patterns.name: Broken 78
patterns.notes: Displaced kick, uneven hats.

patterns.name: Cha-Cha
patterns.notes: Cowbell eighths, congas trading the offbeats.

patterns.name: Mambo
patterns.notes: Bell pattern plus tumbao. The busiest of the presets.

patterns.name: Songo
patterns.notes: Songo's snare-and-conga conversation.

patterns.name: Rock 1
patterns.notes: The plain preset, given four bars of life and a conga fill.

patterns.name: Rock 2
patterns.notes: Busier hat and an extra kick before the backbeat.

patterns.name: Slow Rock
patterns.notes: Twelve-feel ballad. Hat in threes.

patterns.name: Swing
patterns.notes: Ride-style cymbal in triplet feel with shuffle at 80.

patterns.name: Shuffle
patterns.notes: Swung eighths, tambourine on the skips.

patterns.name: Waltz Feel
patterns.notes: Three-feel mapped onto 16 steps so it phases nicely over 64.

patterns.name: Bossa Nova
patterns.notes: Clave over maracas sixteenths. Strict to stay authentic.

patterns.name: Rhumba
patterns.notes: Rhumba clave with a tumbao conga underneath.

patterns.name: Tango
patterns.notes: Dotted tango accent figure. Deliberately rigid.

patterns.name: Beguine
patterns.notes: Soft two-feel with bongo colour.

patterns.name: Synth-Pop 78
patterns.notes: Tambourine doubling the snare — the CR-78 pop sound.

patterns.name: City Pop
patterns.notes: Slinky kick, a touch of shuffle, bright tambourine.

patterns.name: Boogie 78
patterns.notes: Early-80s boogie with cowbell punctuation.

patterns.name: Lo-Fi
patterns.notes: Swung, soft, slightly late. Tone controls rolled down.

patterns.name: Downtempo
patterns.notes: Unhurried. Cymbal set long.

patterns.name: Trip-Hop 78
patterns.notes: Late snare, flams in the fill bar.

patterns.name: Guaguanco
patterns.notes: Three congas in dialogue over clave.

patterns.name: Plena
patterns.notes: Guiro on the offbeats, panderos as snare.

patterns.name: Salsa
patterns.notes: Full salsa engine: bell, clave, tumbao, maracas.

patterns.name: Afrobeat
patterns.notes: Tony Allen displacement — nothing lands where you expect.

patterns.name: Bembe 6/8
patterns.notes: Standard 12/8 bell pattern. Strict — the phasing is the interest.

patterns.name: Calypso
patterns.notes: Two-feel calypso with bongo accents.

patterns.name: One Drop
patterns.notes: Reggae one drop: nothing on beat 1, everything on beat 3.

patterns.name: Dub
patterns.notes: Almost empty, long decays. Leave room for the delay.

patterns.name: Nyabinghi
patterns.notes: Hand-drum three-feel, no hats at all.

patterns.name: Conga Workout
patterns.notes: All four hand drums, each on its own figure, tuned apart.

patterns.name: Bongo Cascara
patterns.notes: Cascara on the bongos with clave underneath.

patterns.name: Clave & Maracas
patterns.notes: Two voices and a kick. A study in restraint.

patterns.name: Reggaeton 78
patterns.notes: Maracas smoothing out the dembow.

patterns.name: Poly 3:4
patterns.notes: Bell in threes, maracas in fives, kick in fours. Strict so the phasing is clean.

patterns.name: Poly 5
patterns.notes: Fives against sevens against fours — a different alignment every bar.

patterns.name: Free Percussion
patterns.notes: Four hand drums interlocking with no obvious downbeat. Flams add hand-drum grace notes.
